dishes.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead; the baked buns keep 1 day airtight and reheat well, or freeze them for a month

steps.text: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and 1 tsp of the salt with the warm milk, melted butter and egg for the dough, and knead until smooth.
Cover and prove until doubled. Meanwhile boil the eggs for the filling for 9 minutes, and cook the cabbage and onion slowly in the butter until soft and sweet.
Season the cabbage with the rest of the salt and the pepper, cool a little, then mix in the chopped eggs and dill.
Divide the dough into 16, flatten each piece, fill, pinch closed and set seam side down on lined trays.
Rest the buns while the oven heats to 200C.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake until golden.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the yoghurt dip up to 1 day ahead; slice the onions in the morning but fry just before serving

steps.text: Toss the onions with the salt and leave to soften.
Stir in the chickpea flour, rice flour, cumin, turmeric, chilli powder, green chilli and coriander, then add the water to make a thick, sticky batter.
Blend the yoghurt with the mint, coriander for the dip and lime juice.
Heat the oil to 175C in a deep pan.
Fry heaped spoonfuls of batter in batches until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with the yoghurt.

dishes.make_ahead: Cook the lamb in its broth up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge; cook the rice and fry the topping on the night

ingredients.item: onions, sliced, one kept for the topping

steps.text: Rinse the rice and leave it to soak.
Brown the lamb in batches in 2 tbsp of the oil.
Add two of the onions and cook until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, spices, dried limes, tomatoes, tomato paste and salt.
Add the water, cover and simmer until the lamb is tender.
Lift out the lamb and keep warm. Measure 750ml of the broth back into the pot, add the drained rice, cover and cook on low.
Rest the rice off the heat. Meanwhile fry the last onion in the rest of the oil until deep brown, adding the almonds and sultanas at the end.
Pile the rice on a platter and top with the lamb, onions, almonds, sultanas and coriander.

veg.make_ahead: Brown the cauliflower and make the spiced chickpea base up to 1 day ahead; cook the rice and fry the topping on the night

ingredients.item: onions, sliced, one kept for the topping

steps.text: Rinse the rice and leave it to soak.
Brown the cauliflower in 2 tbsp of the oil and set aside.
Cook two of the onions in the pan until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, spices, dried limes, tomatoes, tomato paste and salt.
Add the chickpeas and stock and simmer.
Stir in the drained rice and cauliflower, cover and cook on low until the stock is absorbed.
Rest the rice off the heat. Meanwhile fry the last onion in the rest of the oil until deep brown, adding the almonds and sultanas at the end.
Pile the rice on a platter and top with the onions, almonds, sultanas and coriander.

dishes.make_ahead: Slice the mushrooms up to 1 day ahead

steps.text: Brown the sliced mushrooms in half the butter in batches and lift out.
Fry the sliced onion and garlic in the rest of the butter for 5 minutes, then stir in the paprika and flour.
Add the stock and mustard, put the mushrooms back and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the sour cream off the heat.
Cook the noodles, drain and toss with a little butter.
Serve over the noodles with dill and pickles on the side.

dishes.make_ahead: Best fried and eaten the same night; the batter can prove slowly in the fridge for up to 8 hours

steps.text: Soak the saffron in the warm milk.
Whisk the flour, cornflour, yeast, sugar, cardamom and salt with the saffron milk and warm water into a thick, smooth batter.
Cover and leave until bubbly and doubled.
Heat the oil to 175C in a deep pan.
Drop in small spoonfuls of batter in batches and fry, turning, until deep golden.
Drain, toss with the warmed date syrup and scatter with sesame seeds.

dishes.make_ahead: Make the cardamom syrup up to 1 week ahead and blend the mango up to 1 day ahead, both in the fridge; shake to order

steps.text: Simmer the sugar, water and cardamom until dissolved, then cool and strain.
Blend the mango until smooth.
Shake the gin, mango, lime juice and syrup hard with ice, in two batches.
Strain into four tall glasses of ice, top with soda and garnish with lime wheels.

af.make_ahead: Brew and chill the tea and make the cardamom syrup up to 2 days ahead; blend the mango up to 1 day ahead and shake to order

steps.text: Steep the tea bags in the boiling water for 4 minutes and lift them out. Simmer the sugar, water and cardamom until dissolved, then strain. Chill both.
Blend the mango until smooth.
Shake the tea, mango, lime juice and syrup hard with ice, in two batches.
Strain into four tall glasses of ice, top with tonic and garnish with lime wheels.

s.note: Soft baked buns filled with buttery cabbage, onion, egg and dill
s.how: Mix 500g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar and 1 tsp salt with 250ml warm milk, 60g melted butter and 1 egg, and knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove for an hour until doubled. Meanwhile boil 2 eggs for 9 minutes, and cook 500g finely shredded white cabbage and 1 diced onion slowly in 40g butter for 25 minutes until soft and sweet. Season with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp pepper, cool, then mix in the chopped eggs and 2 tbsp chopped dill. Divide the dough into 16, flatten each, fill, pinch closed and set seam side down on lined trays. Rest 15 minutes, brush with beaten egg and bake at 200C for 18 minutes until golden.

s.note: Crisp spiced onion fritters in chickpea batter with mint and coriander yoghurt
s.how: Toss 3 thinly sliced onions with 1 tsp salt and leave 10 minutes. Stir in 150g chickpea flour, 2 tbsp rice flour, 1 tsp each of ground cumin, turmeric and chilli powder, 1 chopped green chilli and half a cup of chopped coriander, then add about 100ml water to make a thick, sticky batter. Blend 200g Greek yoghurt with half a cup each of mint and coriander leaves and the juice of a lime. Heat 1 litre vegetable oil to 175C and fry heaped spoonfuls in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp. Drain and serve hot with the yoghurt.

m.note: Emirati spiced rice with slow-cooked lamb, dried lime, cardamom and tomato, topped with fried onion, sultanas and almonds
m.how: Rinse 400g basmati rice and leave it to soak. Brown 1kg boneless lamb shoulder in 5cm pieces in 2 tbsp vegetable oil, then add 2 sliced onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft. Stir in 4 crushed garlic cloves, 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 tsp each of ground cumin and coriander, 1 tsp turmeric, 1 cinnamon stick, 6 cracked cardamom pods, 2 pierced dried limes, 2 chopped tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato paste and 1.5 tsp salt. Add 1.5 litres water, cover and simmer for 75 minutes until the lamb is tender. Lift out the lamb and keep warm. Measure 750ml of the broth back into the pot, add the drained rice, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes. Fry 1 sliced onion in 1 tbsp oil until deep brown, adding 50g slivered almonds and 50g sultanas at the end. Pile the rice on a platter with the lamb, onions, almonds, sultanas and coriander.

w.note: Crisp cardamom and saffron dumplings tossed in warm date syrup and toasted sesame
w.how: Soak a pinch of saffron threads in 2 tbsp warm milk for 5 minutes. Whisk 250g plain flour, 1 tbsp cornflour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar, 0.5 tsp ground cardamom and a pinch of salt with the saffron milk and 300ml warm water into a thick, smooth batter. Cover and leave for an hour until bubbly and doubled. Heat 1 litre vegetable oil to 175C and drop in small spoonfuls, turning, for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden. Drain, toss with 125ml warm date syrup and scatter with 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds.

d.note: Gin shaken with fresh mango, lime and cardamom syrup, topped with soda over ice
d.how: Simmer 60g caster sugar with 60ml water and 4 crushed cardamom pods until dissolved, then cool and strain. Blend the flesh of 1 large mango until smooth. Shake 240ml gin with the mango, the juice of 2 limes and the syrup with ice, in two batches. Strain into 4 tall glasses of ice, top with 400ml chilled soda water and garnish with lime wheels.
